_doc: BLIND 2016 universe — auditor + pension data as of FY2016 for 33 BBB-tier hospital muni obligors. Two data points per obligor: (1) auditor for FY2016 vs FY2015 (auditor-change detector); (2) DB pension funded ratio as of FY2016 measurement date.
_methodology_warning: BLIND DISCIPLINE: All sources cited are dated 2016-2018 (FY2016 audited financials are typically filed in mid-to-late 2017). NO 2024-2025 era ratings/M&A events used to select or filter obligors. CONTAMINATION DISCLOSURE: While researching, search snippets surfaced post-2017 events for several obligors (e.g., Centegra-Northwestern merger Sept 2018, Presence-Ascension merger March 2018, Adventist HealthCare retiring DB plan, Erlanger 2023 reorganization). These were NOT used to extract FY2016 data points; only the snapshot as known/disclosed as of fiscal-year-end 2016 + audit issuance (late 2017) is recorded here.
_methodology: Researched via (1) ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer for 501(c)(3) hospitals; (2) Federal Audit Clearinghouse references (app.fac.gov); (3) EMMA continuing disclosures (msrb.org); (4) State auditor offices (Tennessee Comptroller, Alabama Examiners, Florida Auditor General, Mississippi state auditor); (5) Hospital own IR pages; (6) Becker's Hospital Review / Bond Buyer 2017 archives. Local pdftotext extraction used where PDF was text-searchable; WebFetch failed for most CID-encoded PDFs.
_critical_limitations: FY2016 historical audit data is extremely difficult to obtain via web search alone — most PDFs from EMMA, state comptrollers, and audit clearinghouses are CID-font-encoded and not text-extractable via WebFetch. ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer surfaces FACs were filed but does not display auditor names in search snippets.
Where auditor name is marked LOW, the data was not directly verified from a primary source dated 2016-2018; relying on detector library would require manual EMMA/FAC retrieval per obligor.

Pension data for 501(c)(3) hospitals is in Note disclosures of audited financials (FASB ASC 715); for public hospital districts (Halifax FL, Hurley MI, Houston County AL, Carson Tahoe NV, Memorial Gulfport MS, Erlanger TN), pension is reported under GASB 68 as Net Pension Liability with Plan Fiduciary Net Position / Total Pension Liability ratio.

For obligors whose pension is part of a multi-employer church plan (e.g., Adventist healthcare entities use AHRP) or state retirement system (Hurley uses MERS, Erlanger uses TCRS), funded ratio cannot be disaggregated for the single obligor — flagged as such.

pension_funded_ratio._notes: Memorial Hospital at Gulfport operates closed DB pension plan. From 10-year Schedule in FY2018 audit: Fiduciary net position as % of total pension liability = 72.00% at 9/30/2016 (vs. 71.40% at 9/30/2017; 68.17% at 9/30/2015). Total pension liability at 9/30/2016 = $142,894,011 (from rollforward). Note: plan_assets_usd and PBO_usd left null because GASB 68 reports net pension liability with plan fiduciary net position (FNP) and total pension liability (TPL) rather than the FASB 'plan assets / PBO' framing; the 72.00% ratio is the directly disclosed funded ratio.

_summary_for_caller.key_finding: Manual FAC/EMMA PDF retrieval would be required to fully verify all 33 obligors. Search-result snippets and ProPublica metadata do not surface auditor firm names. WebFetch fails for most CID-encoded audit PDFs.
_summary_for_caller.recommended_next_action: If detector library requires HIGH confidence on auditor-change signal, consider scripting FAC API access (https://app.fac.gov/dissemination/) which returns structured auditor metadata in JSON. For pension data, GASB-reporting public hospitals (Halifax, Hurley, Erlanger, Memorial Gulfport, Houston County, Carson Tahoe) require schedule-of-changes extraction, while FASB-reporting 501(c)(3) hospitals require Note disclosures.
